newsitem.title: UK: Unilever slips on ice cream worries.
newsitem.headline: Unilever slips on ice cream worries.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever slipped on Tuesday as worries about ice-cream sales emerged and one broker reiterated its "sell" stance on the stock, traders said.
Unilever shares slid 25p to 1381-1/2p by 1200 GMT, after hitting a record high of 1,412p earlier in the session.
Kleinwort Benson said it had reiterated its "sell" stance after limp results from fellow ice-cream maker Treats.
Frozen confectionery-maker Treats Group Plc said pre-tax profits fell to 1.51 million stg for the six months to 29 June, compared with 1.67 milion stg in the previous year.

Treats added that market research showed industry sales of hand-held ice creams and lollies had fallen 26 percent for the eight months to 25 August, compared with last year. Treats' year-on-year sales slipped four percent in the same period.

"This is a significant factor for Unilever as around 20 percent of profits come from European ice-cream and for the third quarter 30 percent will come from ice-cream," said Michael Smith, equity analyst at Kleinwort Benson, who added he expected Q3 results to be disappointing.
But Kleinwort Benson said it would maintain its pretax profit forecasts for 1996 at 2,537 million stg.
On a wider scale, analysts said the addition of co-chairman Niall FitzGerald and his plans to restructure the sprawling empire were encouraging.
"But in terms of fundamentals, nothing much has changed and they're still a low growth company," said Smith.

Difficult sectors such as margarine and detergents will continue to challenge Unilever and until the group secures a position in European growth sectors, it will struggle to meet growth targets, he added.
